bug_description.original: A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) exists in mpz_get_int (mrbgems/mruby-bigint/core/bigint.c): the function can read past the allocated bigint limb array (e.g. accessing y->p[1] beyond the allocation). This can be triggered during bigint comparisons (mrb_bint_cmp / num_gt) and may lead to crashes or other undefined behavior.
bug_description.normalized: The exact 32-byte Ruby-script witness is parsed as text, preserves the leading decimal literal `84467440737095188888` as an `IREP_TT_BIGINT` constant, executes bigint exponentiation with exponent `0`, and then compares that result against ordinary integer `2` with `>`. The exponent-zero path in `mpz_pow` calls `mpz_set_int(..., 1L)`, and `mpz_set_int` correctly allocates only one limb for value `1`. Later `mrb_bint_cmp` tries to convert that single-limb bigint back to `mrb_int` through `mpz_get_int`. Vulnerable `mpz_get_int` checks `digits(y) > 2 || y->p[1] > 1` without first proving that a second limb exists, so when `digits(y) == 1` it still evaluates `y->p[1] > 1` and reads one limb past the 8-byte heap allocation. The fix caches `digits(y)` in `d` and guards the second-limb read with `d == 2`.

source.description: The compiler materializes the oversized attacker-controlled decimal token into an `IREP_TT_BIGINT` pool entry, preserving the exact digit bytes and bigint base metadata that runtime later uses to instantiate the live `mpz_t` value.
source.value_from: The saved `poc` bytes 0..19 are ASCII `84467440737095188888`. This 20-digit literal exceeds the normal integer range for the staged build, so code generation stores it in the bigint literal pool as `[len, base, digits...]` instead of emitting an immediate fixnum.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `mpz_pow(..., 0)` produced a one-limb bigint, this condition still evaluates `y->p[1] > 1`, so the second-limb probe reads 8 bytes past the single-limb heap allocation.

root_cause.description: The original guard conflates 'has more than two digits' with 'may inspect the second limb'. When `digits(y) == 1`, the first disjunct is false but the code still evaluates `y->p[1] > 1`. The patch fixes this exact missing obligation by caching `d = digits(y)` and only touching `y->p[1]` when `d == 2`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled decimal literal is copied into the bigint constant pool and later reloaded by `OP_LOADL` to create the runtime bigint operand.

parser_admitted.description: Format gate for text-vs-bytecode loading. The staged witness is not a `RITE` binary and contains no NUL byte in its 32-byte prefix, so mruby admits it to the text Ruby parser path.
parser_admitted.condition: For this exact witness, `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt` takes the text-script branch rather than the `.mrb` bytecode branch.

admitted_location.code: return mrb_load_exec(mrb, mrb_parse_file_continue(mrb, fp, leading.b, bufsize, c), c);

fine_trace.note: Source. The compiler copies the attacker-controlled 20-digit literal `84467440737095188888` into a bigint pool record that carries its length, base, and digit bytes for later execution.
When the bigint literal is executed, `OP_LOADL` reloads the pooled `[len, base, digits]` record and materializes a runtime `RBigint` from those attacker-controlled bytes.
The witness executes `** 0` on that bigint value, so bigint exponentiation is invoked on the runtime operand from step 2 with exponent `0` from the same expression.
Control decision. Because the script exponent is exactly `0`, `mpz_pow` takes its constant-one fast path instead of multiplying the original bigint.
The exponent-zero branch materializes the comparison result as bigint value `1` by delegating to `mpz_set_int`.
For integer value `1`, the high-limb test is false, so `mpz_set_int` derives `len = 1`: the result needs exactly one limb.
`mpz_set_int` allocates storage for exactly one `mp_limb`. ASan's allocation trace shows this path reaches `mpz_realloc`, which returns the 8-byte heap region later overread in `mpz_get_int`.
The later `>` compares the bigint result from step 5 against ordinary integer literal `2`, so comparison takes the non-bigint-right-hand-side path that converts the left bigint back to `mrb_int`.
That comparison path invokes `mpz_get_int` on the one-limb bigint from step 7, making the single-limb layout relevant to the subsequent conversion checks.
For the bigint value `1`, `digits(y)` returns `1`: only limb `p[0]` exists and is nonzero.

Root cause. With `digits(y) == 1`, the first disjunct `digits(y) > 2` is false, but the vulnerable source has no `digits(y) == 2` guard before the second-limb test. The patch introduces exactly that missing check.

Sink. Evaluating the second disjunct reads limb index 1 even though step 7 allocated only one limb. AddressSanitizer reports this as a heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at `bigint.c:749:29`, 0 bytes past the 8-byte region allocated in `mpz_realloc`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: No. The one-limb allocation at `mpz_realloc` is correct for value `1`; the bug is the later missing `d == 2` guard before reading `y->p[1]`.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The fix rewrites `mpz_get_int` to cache `d = digits(y)`, reject `d > 2`, test `y->p[1]` only under `d == 2`, and compute the one-limb case from `y->p[0]` alone. That is exactly the obligation missing at step 11.

format.name: Ruby source file
format.contract: A text Ruby script admitted by `mrb_load_detect_file_cxt` as source code, with the exact leading decimal literal `84467440737095188888`, an executed exponent literal `0` on the `**` path, and an executed `>` comparison against ordinary integer literal `2`, so mruby creates a single-limb bigint result `1` and then routes that value through `mpz_get_int`.
